The contracting authority will facilitate access to relevant documentation and key stakeholders. 4.2 Steering of the evaluation The reference person for the evaluation will be the Programme Coordinator. The evaluation process will be supported by members of the MEAL working group, who will provide guidance on methodological and organisational aspects and monitor coherence and quality throughout the process. The Programme Steering Group will be responsible for selecting the evaluator(s), monitoring the evaluation process and validating the evaluation report(s) and management response(s). For practical reasons, specific tasks may be delegated to a smaller group reporting back to the Programme Steering Group. 6 4.3 Methodological Orientation Given the complexity o

youth sensitivity: The evaluation should pay due attention to gender justice and the participation and inclusion of youth as actors of change. • Participation and respect : The evaluation process should promote respectful engagement with stakeholders and recognise the knowledge and perspectives of partner organisations, rights holders and participants. 5. Expected outputs The evaluation shall meet the quality criteria of the OECD-DAC, as provided for in Article 44 of the Royal Decree of 11 September 2016 on non-governmental cooperation. The evaluation shall also explicitly address the evaluation questions outlined in these Terms of Reference. The evaluation will be procured through a single public procurement procedure divided into three lots. Each lot constitutes a separate evaluation assignment and may be awarded to a different evaluator or evaluation team. The deliverables described below apply to each lot awarded. The following deliverables are expected: 1. Inception Report: The evaluator(s) shall submit one concise inception report for each awarded lot, detailing the proposed evaluation methodology, data collection and analysis methods, work plan and timeline. The inception report should demonstrate how the proposed approach will address the evaluation questions

lan and timeline. The inception report should demonstrate how the proposed approach will address the evaluation questions and account for the complexity of the programme's change processes. 2. Evaluation Reports : The evaluator(s) shall submit one evaluation report for each outcome included in the awarded lot(s). Reports should be written in an accessible style and include at least: 7 • An executive summary of maximum five pages that can be shared with relevant stakeholders; • A description of the methodology and tools used, including their limitations; • Findings addressing the evaluation questions outlined in these Terms of Reference; • Conclusions; • Concrete and realistic recommendations. Reports should be concise and should normally not exceed 40 pages, excluding annexes. 3. Sense-making workshop : The evaluator(s) shall facilitate at least one sense -making workshop for each awarded lot, involving relevant representatives of Broederlijk Delen, Studio Globo and partner organisations. Where appropriate, a single workshop may cover several outcomes within the same lot. The workshop should provide an opportunity to discuss the evaluation findings, validate factual accuracy and interpretations, and reflect on the relevance and feasibility of the recommendations
